tema: Uses eLORETA to characterize changes in current density in the central autonomic network (CAN) after exercise in ME/CFS as a model of PEM.
diseno: Pilot study with resting EEG before, after and 24 h after submaximal isometric handgrip exercise in 7 ME/CFS patients and 6 healthy controls.
hallazgos: There were significant differences immediately after the test, more marked at 24 h, especially in the low alpha (8-10 Hz) and low beta (13-18 Hz) sub-bands. Both groups showed baseline changes at 24 h.
conclusion: Preliminary evidence of CAN involvement in PEM; CAN current density could serve as an index of PEM and eLORETA is a feasible tool.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree on CAN, PEM and eLORETA; the conclusions (from the discussion) are more cautious, stressing the sample size and the exclusion of subcortical regions.

tema: Evaluates whether a short (15 min) tilt test at 20 degrees is enough to provoke a reduction in cerebral blood flow (CBF) in patients with severe ME/CFS.
diseno: Exploratory study in 19 patients with severe ME/CFS (18 women) with OI in daily life; extracranial Doppler of the internal carotid and vertebral arteries, cardiac index and end-tidal CO2.
hallazgos: CBF fell from 617 to 452 ml/min (27% decrease) and cardiac index by 26%; all 19 patients met criteria for abnormal CBF reduction. Heart rate increased and stroke volume and end-tidal CO2 decreased.
conclusion: A 20-degree test for 15 min is sufficient to provoke a clinically significant reduction in CBF in severe ME/CFS, comparable to that of the standard 70-degree test, and can improve its assessment.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on CBF, tilt test and severity; the conclusions add that POTS is a small subgroup and that CBF abnormalities appear without heart rate or blood pressure abnormalities.

tema: Investigates the role of cerebral blood flow (CBF) and HRV in modulating pain and symptoms of CFS under physical and emotional stress.
diseno: Randomized controlled crossover study at the University Hospital of Brussels; 20 CFS patients and 20 sedentary controls; temporal summation of pressure pain, CBF with transcranial Doppler and HRV by digital plethysmography during light exercise and emotional stress.
hallazgos: There was no group effect or interaction in CBF or HRV; both changed with exercise with no differences between groups. Temporal summation pain at the trapezius decreased after exercise in controls (p = 0.037) but not in patients (p = 0.108), suggesting altered pain modulation; there were no correlations with symptoms.
conclusion: The results appear to refute previous CBF/HRV alterations in CFS; these parameters would not explain pain before, during and after exercise.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent with a mostly negative result; the abstract acknowledges small sample and light exercise as limitations. The keywords include pain modulation and emotional stress, aligned with the design.

tema: Measures cerebral blood flow during the tilt test in ME/CFS to check whether it is reduced even without hypotension or tachycardia.
diseno: Controlled study with 429 ME/CFS patients (247 with normal haemodynamic response, 62 with delayed orthostatic hypotension, 120 with POTS) and 44 healthy controls; 30-min tilt test with carotid and vertebral Doppler and a 15-symptom OI questionnaire.
hallazgos: The reduction in CBF at the end of the test was 7% in controls versus 26% in ME/CFS (24% with normal response, 28% with delayed hypotension, 29% with POTS). 82%, 98% and 100% respectively showed abnormal reduction, and OI symptoms correlated with the reduction in CBF.
conclusion: CBF is reduced in ME/CFS during the tilt test, even without heart rate or blood pressure abnormalities, and its measurement can improve the evaluation of OI.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are fully consistent; all three reinforce the relationship between OI symptoms and CBF reduction and the value of extracranial Doppler in patients with apparently normal haemodynamics.

tema: Examines the recovery of cerebral blood flow after the tilt test in ME/CFS and its risk factors.
diseno: Study in 60 adults with ME/CFS (30 with normal response, 4 with delayed orthostatic hypotension, 26 with POTS); extracranial Doppler before, at the end of and 5 min after the test, cardiac index by suprasternal Doppler and end-tidal CO2; mild, moderate or severe disease.
hallazgos: The CBF reduction was 29% at the end of the test and persisted at 16% after 5 min supine, even though cardiac index normalized. The post-test reduction depended on severity (mild 7%, moderate 16%, severe 25%) and not on the haemodynamic pattern or hypocapnia.
conclusion: CBF recovery after orthostatic stress is incomplete and related to clinical severity, which could influence recommendations on energy management and lying down after a stressor.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on CBF, POTS and severity; the conclusion (taken from the abstract) adds practical implications not present in the keywords. The abstract appears truncated at the end.

tema: Explores whether there is a physiological link between cerebral vascular control and skeletal muscle pH handling in CFS.
diseno: Study with 17 consecutive CFS patients (Fukuda criteria); CBF and muscle pH at rest with MRI and 31P MR spectroscopy; fMRI during Valsalva manoeuvre and 31P-MRS during plantar flexion exercise.
hallazgos: There was an inverse correlation between CBF and muscle pH at rest (r = -0.67; p < 0.01) and prolonged cerebral vasoconstriction in the sympathetic phase of the Valsalva was associated with higher muscle pH after exercise (r = 0.69; p < 0.008).
conclusion: Cerebral vascular control is closely related to muscle pH at rest and after dynamic stimulation, indicating a strong influence of autonomic dysfunction.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the discussion qualifies that the results are correlational and do not prove causality, and calls for more studies on muscle oxygenation and perfusion.

tema: Analyses DNA methylation profiles in PBMC of ME/CFS patients compared with controls.
diseno: Case-control study in a New Zealand cohort (10 patients and 10 controls matched for age and sex); RRBS sequencing analysed with DMAP and MethylKit.
hallazgos: 76 fragments and 394 differentially methylated cytosines were identified, and 122 genes with differential methylation in the gene body. 59% of those genes coincided with previous array-based studies, and 30 enriched pathways were immune, metabolic and neurological.
conclusion: Methylation patterns clearly distinguish patients from controls. The neurotransmitter and neuropeptide pathways point to an altered neurological pathophysiology.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent (methylation, PBMC, gene body). The conclusions come from the structured abstract itself, so they offer no independent view; the abstract appears truncated at the end.

tema: Characterizes the effect of IL-2 stimulation and pharmacological modulation of TRPM7 on NK cytotoxicity in ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study: 17 patients and 17 matched controls; cytotoxicity assays by flow cytometry and colocalization of TRPM7 with PIP2 and cortical actin by confocal microscopy.
hallazgos: Preliminary results indicate that there is crosstalk between IL-2 and TRPM7 in NK cells.
conclusion: Together with previous studies of TRP dysfunction, the data support a possible channelopathy as a mechanism of ME/CFS, although a larger sample and techniques such as patch-clamp are needed.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions go somewhat beyond the abstract in proposing channelopathy as a pathomechanism, despite the preliminary nature.

tema: Qualitatively characterizes the experience of PEM in daily life and after a CPET in ME/CFS patients.
diseno: Nine focus groups with 43 patients with self-reported ME/CFS (2016-2019); thematic analysis supported by qualitative software.
hallazgos: Three main themes emerged (exhaustion, cognitive difficulties and neuromuscular complaints) with great individual variation. Of 18 participants who answered about the CPET, 17 reported symptom onset within 24 h and a peak at 72 h.
conclusion: PEM varies greatly between individuals; fixed quantitative questionnaires may not capture it and a mixed approach is required. Identifying PEM subtypes could guide treatments.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent. The PDF conclusions add the life impact of PEM (complete rest, hopelessness) and the idea of subtypes, absent from the abstract.

tema: Characterizes the fatigue associated with primary Sjögren's syndrome and its overlap with ME/CFS.
diseno: Cross-sectional study in 19 patients with primary Sjögren's: severity and activity questionnaires, Canadian Criteria, repeated handgrip strength and autoantibodies against α1, α2, β1, β2, M3 and M4 receptors.
hallazgos: A subgroup with severe fatigue had more pain, depression and sleep disturbances; 4 of 18 met the CCC; handgrip strength correlated with fatigue but recovered within an hour; β1, β2 and M4 antibodies correlated with activity (ESSDAI), not with fatigue.
conclusion: The absence of PEM triggered by physical exertion distinguishes Sjögren's from ME/CFS, physical activity does not appear to worsen fatigue in Sjögren's and autoantibodies could mediate its manifestations.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions add the practical implication regarding physical activity and the figure of 22% who would meet the CCC.

tema: Systematic review comparing the symptoms and pathogenesis of post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome (PTLDS) with ME/CFS.
diseno: Systematic review with qualitative analysis of 18 studies on PTLDS symptoms.
hallazgos: Most PTLDS studies recorded at least four of the six major ME/CFS symptoms (impaired activity and fatigue >6 months, PEM, unrefreshing sleep); one recorded 26 of the 29 symptoms; overall all but three were cited.
conclusion: PTLDS and ME/CFS appear to share pathogenesis despite different infectious origins, since both arise after an infectious event from which ~10% do not recover.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions include a comparative symptom table (noise) and provide no mechanistic data to support the suggested common pathogenesis.

tema: Compares autoimmunity profiles in chronic fatigue of different aetiology (viral, stress-related, idiopathic).
diseno: Case-control study: 33 CFS/ME patients in three subgroups (herpesvirus carriers, stress, idiopathic) versus 20 healthy donors with or without burnout fatigue; 36 neural and visceral autoantigens by ELI-test ELISA.
hallazgos: Anti-β2-glycoprotein I antibodies were elevated in patients; autoantibodies against double-stranded DNA and collagen increased; the viral subgroup showed antibodies against calcium channels and the stress subgroup against dopamine, glutamate, GABA and NF200 receptors.
conclusion: There are autoimmune reactions against neural and adrenal medulla antigens in all subtypes; visceral symptoms could be secondary to autoimmune dysautonomia and a link with antiphospholipid syndrome is suggested.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions add the context of post-COVID syndrome and a limitations section on the pooled control serum.

tema: Analyses the item content of the ME/CFS Common Data Elements (CDEs) using the WHO ICF framework.
diseno: Content analysis: 119 CDEs reviewed, 38 included (944 items linked to 1503 ICF concepts) by independent reviewers.
hallazgos: 73.65% of the concepts corresponded to Body Functions (fatigability, energy, sleep, emotions, pain); Activities and Participation accounted for 25.62% and Environmental Factors for 0.73%.
conclusion: Few items assess the impact on activities and participation; ME/CFS-specific PROMs, item banks and computerized adaptive tests need to be developed, informed by qualitative research.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions expand on the abstract by noting the burden of multiple assessments and the relevance for long COVID (PASC).

tema: Compares the reduction in cerebral blood flow during orthostatic stress in ME/CFS patients with and without joint hypermobility.
diseno: Case-control study: 100 women with ME/CFS and joint hypermobility versus 100 without hypermobility, matched for age and duration; tilt test with CBF measurement.
hallazgos: Hypermobile patients had more POTS and a greater reduction in CBF (-32% vs -23%; p<0.0001), a difference present with both POTS and a normal haemodynamic response.
conclusion: Joint hypermobility is associated with greater CBF reductions during orthostatic stress, independently of the heart rate and blood pressure response; the underlying mechanisms remain to be studied.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree; the conclusions are somewhat more cautious in pointing out that mechanisms such as vascular laxity, proposed in the abstract, remain unstudied.

tema: Evaluates the transcriptomic changes induced by an exercise test designed to provoke PEM in women with ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study in women with ME/CFS and healthy controls, with samples before exercise, at maximal effort and during recovery; transcriptomic analysis. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: At maximal effort the patients showed no significant expression changes, whereas the controls altered gene networks of immune function. In recovery, the patients showed dysregulated immune signalling pathways and dysfunctional cellular stress responses.
conclusion: Patients fail to achieve the transcriptomic adjustments that allow recovery from exertion; their immune cells show dysfunctional cytokine networks and vulnerability to apoptosis. The findings could guide diagnosis and targeted treatments.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on PEM, stress response and immune dysregulation. The conclusions add epigenetic regulation of apoptotic pathways and vulnerability to cell death, which do not appear in the abstract.

tema: Develops a PLS-DA diagnostic model for ME/CFS that integrates miRNA, blood tests and extracellular vesicle characteristics.
diseno: PLS-DA model with 817 initial variables (demographic, laboratory, PBMC and extracellular vesicle miRNA, and vesicle characteristics), complemented with Raman microspectroscopy of the vesicles. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: The model selected 5 components and 32 regressors, among them 4 vesicle characteristics. Raman identified carotenoid peaks as a fingerprint of ME/CFS, with little diagnostic capacity on its own (AUC = 0.7067), but helped reduce the miRNAs while maintaining perfect classification (AUC = 1).
conclusion: Blood vesicles carry relevant information about the disease; the authors call for validating the model in larger cohorts and identifying the components detected by Raman.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree (extracellular vesicles, miRNA, PLS-DA, Raman). The conclusions text (discussion) is noise (contributions, funding, acknowledgements) and provides no conclusions.

tema: Reviews the similarities between CFS and chronic pain as altered protective systems from a biopsychosocial approach.
diseno: Narrative review; search methodology not stated.
hallazgos: Pain and fatigue are protective sensations that become problems when they become chronic; both syndromes share symptoms and pathophysiological findings (sustained activation); the predictive brain model would explain the usefulness of CBT and stress-reduction therapies.
conclusion: Pain and fatigue are real experiences with peripheral and brain causes; a holistic approach that also treats comorbidities (sleep, psychiatric) offers effective treatment and should be prioritized in the health system.
triangulacion: Keywords (biopsychosocial model, CBT), abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions (from the discussion) add physical activity, mindfulness and sleep treatment. A psychosomatic perspective that contrasts with other works in the batch.

tema: Narrative review of the pathophysiology, clinical features and treatment of ME/CFS, highlighting the osteopathic approach.
diseno: Narrative review; no own population.
hallazgos: Describes the disease (PEM, fatigue, unrefreshing sleep, cognitive impairment, immune and autonomic dysfunction) and the challenges: absence of diagnostic markers, divergent criteria and lack of medical knowledge.
conclusion: ME/CFS is multifactorial and without known biomarkers; more research and awareness are needed, and osteopathic medicine could provide temporary relief.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions are cautious in limiting the osteopathic benefit to temporary relief.

tema: Evaluates whether symptoms in the first two weeks of COVID-19 predict the development of ME/CFS at 6 months.
diseno: Random forest predictive models with the 54-item DePaul Symptom Questionnaire; sample size not stated in the available text.
hallazgos: Early symptoms, especially of PEM, predicted ME/CFS with an accuracy of 94.6%; a reduced eight-symptom model reached 93.5%.
conclusion: Several IOM diagnostic criteria present in the first weeks after COVID-19 predict long COVID and ME/CFS at 6 months; why PEM is the greatest predictor should be investigated.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree on PEM and prediction; the conclusions (from the discussion) are more cautious: they point to recall bias, a non-diverse sample and non-medical diagnosis.

tema: Identifies predictors of ME/CFS after infectious mononucleosis in university students using pre-illness data.
diseno: Prospective cohort of 4501 students: 238 developed mononucleosis and were followed for 6 months; behavioural and psychological surveys and cytokines at three time points; 67 asymptomatic individuals as controls.
hallazgos: 55 of 238 (23%) met ME/CFS criteria at 6 months; before the mononucleosis, the severe ME/CFS group did not differ in stress, coping, anxiety or depression, but did in behavioural measures and had less IL-6 and IL-13; during the infection it had more IL-12 and less IL-13.
conclusion: Those who developed ME/CFS had at baseline more physical symptoms and immune irregularities, but not more psychological symptoms.
triangulacion: The conclusions come from the structured abstract and agree with it; the keywords (mononucleosis, risk factors, IL-6) reflect the study well.

tema: To present current knowledge on chronic fatigue in patients with iron metabolism disorders.
diseno: Narrative review based on PubMed, Scopus and Wiley.
hallazgos: Fatigue is a prominent symptom in both iron deficiency and iron overload, and its management in these patients is not well defined.
conclusion: More research is needed on the role of iron in fatigue and on the validation of fatigue scales, especially in iron overload.
triangulacion: Consistent; the focus is chronic fatigue as a symptom, not ME/CFS as an entity. The conclusions (with administrative noise) propose studying non-transferrin-bound iron.

tema: Examines the PBMC proteome of ME/CFS patients using SWATH-MS to understand their pathophysiology.
diseno: Case-control study with a small, well-characterized group of patients (n = 11) and matched controls; SWATH-MS proteomics and PCA to stratify.
hallazgos: PCA separated 9 of the 11 patients from the controls; in that subgroup there were 99 differentially expressed proteins. Many were involved in mitochondrial function, oxidative phosphorylation, the electron transport chain and redox regulation, and others in the inflammatory response, DNA methylation, apoptosis and the proteasome.
conclusion: The results support a model of deficient ATP production with compensation upstream of complex V and increased oxidative stress, which would plausibly explain PEM.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative phosphorylation. The PDF conclusions are more cautious: the diagnostic value of these proteins must be validated in larger cohorts and against similar diseases.

tema: Identifies DNA methylation patterns associated with ME/CFS in PBMC.
diseno: Case-control study: 13 patients and 12 controls with global methylation (ELISA-type assay) and Illumina MethylationEPIC arrays (about 850,000 CpGs); validation by pyrosequencing in 33 cases and 31 controls from two geographically distant cohorts (Miami and Valencia).
hallazgos: Global methylation was similar between groups, but 17,296 differentially methylated CpGs were detected in 6368 genes and 307 promoters with differential methylation. These were associated with at least 15 pathways, mostly cell signalling with a strong immune component.
conclusion: The results confirm DNA methylation as an epigenetic mechanism associated with ME/CFS and agree with immune dysregulation. Larger cohorts are needed before using it as a diagnostic marker.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on methylation, CpGs and immune dysregulation. The conclusions add the need to assess the effect on gene expression; the rest of the text is supplementary tables.

tema: Explores multisite photoplethysmography as a possible diagnostic biomarker of CFS based on the peripheral pulse response to standing.
diseno: Pilot study with 14 CFS patients and 14 age-matched sedentary controls; photoplethysmography at the ears, fingers and toes during supine rest and 3 min of tilting at 70 degrees.
hallazgos: The CFS group showed a smaller pulse transit time response (median change 26% vs 37%; p=0.002), with no differences in amplitude, although this correlated weakly with fatigue severity. The area under the ROC curve was 0.81 and the diagnostic accuracy 82%.
conclusion: Pulse wave abnormalities could be an objective measure to differentiate CFS from controls, but larger and better characterized studies are required.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the autonomic focus and on photoplethysmography; the discussion is more cautious (pilot study, no causality) and links the findings to cerebral autoregulation and the overlap with POTS.

tema: Literature review on dysfunction of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis as a possible neuroendocrine cause of CFS.
diseno: Narrative review; no own population.
hallazgos: Reports a prevalence of up to 422 cases per 100,000 in the US, its economic impact and several causal lines (neurally mediated hypotension, viral pathogens, immune disorders, lymphocyte enzymes, psychological cause).
conclusion: The available conclusions do not correspond to this review: they come from a study on the ATP profile test that implicates mitochondrial dysfunction (Int J Clin Exp Med 2009).
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree on the HPA axis, but the conclusions belong to another article (mitochondrial dysfunction), so there is a source discrepancy and they cannot be triangulated.
